input: Open a custodial investment account for my niece

gold.taskTitle: Open a Custodial Investment Account for Your Niece
gold.taskDescription: Set up a custodial investment account in the user's name on behalf of their niece as the minor beneficiary.

questions.title: How old is your niece right now?
questions.description: The niece's age affects account eligibility rules, contribution limits, and how soon she gains control of the funds.

questions.title: What is the primary purpose of this account?
questions.description: Understanding the goal — college savings, long-term wealth building, a gift — determines the best account type to recommend.

questions.title: Which account type are you considering, UGMA or 529?
questions.description: UGMA accounts allow flexible spending while 529 plans are tax-advantaged but restricted to education expenses; clarifying this shapes the entire plan.

questions.title: Do you have a brokerage or platform already in mind?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user prefers Fidelity, Vanguard, Schwab, or another provider determines the specific steps and forms required.

questions.title: What is your initial deposit amount for this account?
questions.description: The starting contribution amount may affect which platforms or account tiers are available and relevant to the user.

questions.title: Do you have your niece's Social Security number available?
questions.description: A minor's SSN is required by all custodial account providers; not having it is a common blocker that needs to be resolved early.

questions.title: Are your niece's parents aware of and on board with this?
questions.description: Parental awareness can affect the process, especially if the parents need to provide documentation or if there are coordination considerations.
